transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. I'm here because I just keep blowing up at people over absolutely nothing. 

Like, I work in retail, and the other day I yelled at one of my employees just for putting some stock on the wrong shelf. I mean, I really lost it on them. Afterward, I was actually shaking, because... well, that is just not how I usually treat people. I need to figure out why I'm acting like this.
How long have you been experiencing these sudden anger outbursts? Is this something new for you, or have you always been this way?

It's definitely new. I haven't always been this way at all. It's really just been going on for about two weeks now. Um, it started right after we had a kitchen fire... it was during our first weekend working on the house. Ever since then, I've just been having these outbursts.

Besides these anger outbursts, have you been having any other problems since the fire — like unwanted memories of it popping into your head, trouble sleeping, nightmares, or feeling like you need to avoid reminders of what happened?

Yeah, the unwanted memories are definitely happening. The fire just keeps jumping into my head out of nowhere. 

I'll be doing something completely normal, like... picking up a pan, or even just opening a spreadsheet at work, and suddenly I'm right back there. It's like I can actually smell the smoke and see the kitchen filling up before I can even stop it. It just happens before I realize what's going on.
